blurb:
Josie has floppy ears, a nubby little tail, and exactly the kind of energy that needs the right match. She's a hound mix, about six years old and 35 pounds, and she came back to Mostly Mutts after a short adoption because her energy level wasn't a fit for that family. That's not a knock on Josie. It just means she needs someone who actually wants an active dog, not someone who hopes the activity fades over time.

She's playful and genuinely affectionate — graduates walks, then wants the couch spot right next to you. The volunteers say she's got occasional zoomies and rates herself a 5 to 7 on energy depending on the day. She does some mouthy play, never mean, just enthusiastic. Kids 10 and up who want a dog to actually run around with are probably a great fit. She'd need to be your only pet — she hasn't clicked with other dogs or cats.

Josie went through the Prison Pups training program and knows her sit, stay, and then some. She's in a foster home now through Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Come meet her and see if the energy matches yours.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Returned after a short adoption with a self-rated energy scale of 5–7 is both honest and disarmingly charming for readers
• Prison Pups training credential paired with a failed-match backstory positions her as capable but overlooked — a compelling combo
• Short adoption followed by a second wait, with a highly specific ideal-home profile, suggests she has been searching longer than average

blurb:
Someone at the shelter started calling Asher 'goofy and funny' and the name stuck. He's a Boxer-Corgi mix, about three years old and 40 pounds, with a ginger brindle coat and a compact build that makes people do a double-take when they first see him. He graduated from the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, loves to chase a ball, and will actually bring it back — at least as long as you keep throwing it.

He's got some opinions about other dogs in his space. He's fine meeting them on walks and at the shelter, but he's guarded toys and beds before, so he'd do best as your only dog at home. No cats, and kids 15 and up are the right fit since younger kids make him a little nervous and he's got enough bounce to knock someone over without meaning to. Reactive around dogs on leash? His trainer will walk you through it — that's not a dealbreaker, just something to work on together.

If you've got a fenced yard and want a medium-sized dog with a big personality, Asher's worth the drive. He's in a foster home now at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Walk in or reach out to get the process started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Boxer-Corgi build is a visual hook — the double-take description practically writes itself into a shareable newsletter moment
• Prison Pups graduation adds a feel-good community-program angle that broadens reader emotional investment
• Specific household requirements narrow the pool, signaling he has likely been waiting for the right fit for some time

blurb:
Yasmeen's foster mom says her adopters are going to hit the jackpot. That's not a throwaway line — this is an eight-year-old Lab-Terrier mix who came in a little guarded and, within one day of the Prison Pups training program, had completely settled in. She just needed to know she could trust you. Once she does, she's loyal and loving in that quiet, steady way that senior dogs tend to be.

She's done well with other dogs, including a Boxer she stayed with while her foster was on vacation. She's good with cats, too. She met kids as young as seven and gave them kisses. She does have some protective instincts around her people when strangers come into the home — she's worked on it in training and it's improved a lot, but a family with dog-savvy kids 15 and up is probably the smoothest fit. Her trainer will do a proper introduction either way.

If you've wanted a calm, devoted dog who's already past the chaos years, Yasmeen is worth meeting. She's in a foster home now through Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Reach out or stop by to get started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Foster's 'jackpot' quote combined with a one-day trust breakthrough is the strongest emotional hook in the entire candidate pool
• Senior dog who thrives with dogs, cats, and young kids defies the hard-to-place stereotype and delivers a genuinely surprising story
• Eight-year-old Lab mix with protective instincts faces real adoption headwinds, making a newsletter feature the highest-leverage intervention available

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Twiggy had a home for years after being adopted from Mostly Mutts. Then another cat joined the family, they didn't get along, and she ended up back at the rescue. She's about seven years old, roughly 12 pounds, and a tortoiseshell, which if you know tortoiseshells, already tells you something about her personality.

She was pretty spicy when she first came back in. That's understandable. Her whole world got flipped upside down. She's been decompressing in a foster home and the rescue says more personality details are coming soon as she settles in. What they do know: she loves attention from people once she knows you, she's litter trained, spayed, microchipped, current on vaccines, and combo tested negative.

She'd do best as your only cat. Dogs are a maybe depending on the individual dog. Kids are probably fine if they're calm and gentle with her. She's not a from-day-one-on-your-lap cat, but she's not a hide-under-the-bed-forever cat either. She just needs time to trust you, and once she does, she's going to be a real companion.

Adoption fee is $175. Mostly Mutts is foster-based out of Kennesaw, so reach out directly to get the conversation started.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue, no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• The decompression arc — spicy arrival softening into a loyal companion — is a reader-friendly transformation story
• Tortoiseshell personality cue paired with honest nuance will appeal to experienced cat owners who know the type
• Still-settling status and incomplete personality profile suggest a recent return, making timing for a feature strategic

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
Iceman was adopted from Mostly Mutts as a kitten, spent five years with one family, and then their situation changed and he ended up back. Not his fault. Just one of those things. Now he's five years old, 11 pounds, neutered, microchipped, up to date on vaccines, and ready to do it all again with somebody new.

His previous family said he wasn't a fan of other male cats, which is pretty common. He did great with four kids in a foster home a few years back, so children in the house are probably fine as long as they're gentle with him. A female cat housemate could work well. Dogs are unknown territory, so that one would need a meet and greet to figure out.

He's described as a hang-with-his-people kind of cat. Watches the world go by, likes being around you, keeps his area clean. Not a lot of drama. The adoption fee is $175 and he's currently in a foster home in Kennesaw.

Mostly Mutts is a foster-based rescue, so there's no facility to walk into. Reach out by phone or email and they'll get you connected.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue, no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• Five years of proven family life makes him one of the most predictable, low-risk adoption options in the group
• Returned-through-no-fault story is relatable and emotionally resonant for readers who value loyalty
• Second shelter stint after years in a home implies a meaningful wait that deserves spotlight attention

shelter_name: Mostly Mutts Animal Rescue & Adoption, Inc.
blurb:
She came in with her siblings as part of the Go-Gos litter, got adopted, and then came back after a month when her stomach started giving her trouble. No clear diagnosis after months of testing and food changes, just a small cat with a sensitive gut and a foster mom who calls her the best cat ever. That says a lot.

Gina is about 11 months old and roughly five pounds, and her foster says she'll probably stay that way. Independent enough to give you space, but she does love to snuggle when the mood hits. She's playful, she's been good around kids and a leashed dog, and she gets along fine with the two adult cats in her foster home right now.

Here's the honest part: she still vomits sometimes, and that's likely not going to fully go away. If you have other cats, it's manageable with a separate feeding setup since she's on a special diet. It's not a dealbreaker, it's just something to plan around. For the right person, this is a very easy cat with one small asterisk.

Gina is at Mostly Mutts, which is a foster-based rescue out of Kennesaw. Reach out by phone or email to get the process started and set up a meet.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue, no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• Returned adopter with ongoing health mystery creates a genuine underdog narrative readers will root for
• Foster mom's 'best cat ever' endorsement is a powerful trust signal that cuts through the sensitive-stomach caveat
• Months of testing and two shelter stints signal a longer-than-average wait, creating real adoption urgency
